newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ICE rates Zwack as "buy" on better outlook.
newsitem.headline: ICE rates Zwack as "buy" on better outlook.

text.p: Spirits producer Zwack Unicum Rt will boost earnings this year despite a sluggish domestic market, said ICE Securities of London.
ICE Securities recommended the share as a "buy".
The report, by ICE Securities of London, said internal cost-controlling measures had improved the prospects for the company, whose flagship product is the bitter-sweet liqueur Unicum.

"Whilst Zwack still operates in a somewhat depressed domestic legal spirits market, the company, with its greatly improved logistic, inventory and financial control, is certain to maintain its market leader status," analyst Rudi Voros said.

Voros foresaw a waning of the negative impact on consumer spending of the government's 1995 austerity measures and detected signs that the government is beginning to tackle illegal alcohol sales, creating an improved market environment.

"As the purchasing power of the domestic consumers is gradually restored during 1997, we foresee a significant improvement in Zwack's profitability which is not reflected by the current share price," Voros said.
The report forecast a modest increase in sales this year followed by a 26 percent jump in 1997 while income growth will outpace inflation in both years.
It also forecast Zwack to boost net profits to 686 million forints on sales of 13 billion forints in 1996, up from 509 million and 12.37 billion, respectively, in 1995.
For 1997 ICE predicted a net profit of 933 million on sales of 16.4 billion forints.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Zwack shares ended on Monday at 2,850 forints, down 50 in light turnover.
